en: Hi, the results report for {brand} is ready: reach {reach} last month and an engagement rate of {er}. Shall we go through it this week?
Hi, good news: {brand} gained {gain3} followers in three months and stands at {followers}. Thank you for the great content.
Hi, the engagement rate for {brand} is {er} last month and our level is {state}. Can we talk about a new plan?

Hi {brand}, can we meet for 20 minutes to go through your {freq} report?
Hi, {brand} met the goals for {month}: {gain_act} new followers and a reach of {reach_act}. Well done!

Hi, we want to set the goals for the next month for {brand}. Last month: engagement rate {er_act}. Do you agree to aim for {er_goal}?
Hi, our quarterly review for {brand} is on {meeting}. Your accounts gained {gain} followers this quarter. Does the date suit you?
Hi, thank you for the review meeting. For {brand} we agreed: {decision}. We will send the plan this week.
Hi, how happy are you with the results of {brand} this quarter, from 1 to 5? Your answer helps us plan the next quarter.
Hi, our test for {brand} on {platform} is done: {test}. Result: {state}, a lift of {lift}. We will use it in your plan.
Hi, may we run a test for {brand} on {platform}: {test}? It runs for {days} days and costs you nothing extra.
Hi, the test "{test}" for {brand} showed no clear difference ({lift}). We will try a bigger change next.
Hi, {competitor} is ahead of {brand} on {platform} with {followers} followers. Our share of the audience is {share}. Can we plan a catch-up push?
Hi, {brand} leads {competitor} on {platform}: share of audience {share} and a rate gap of {gap}. We will keep the pace.
Hi, {competitor} does this on {platform}: {note}. Shall we try a version for {brand}?
Hi, our recommendation for {brand}: {action}. Reason: {topic}. Do you approve?
Hi, the action "{action}" for {brand} was due on {due} and is still {state}. Can we finish it this week?
Hi, we finished the action "{action}" for {brand}. We will measure the effect and report back.
Hi, {brand} received {leads} leads and {sales} sales from {platform} in {month}, with revenue of {revenue}. Result: {state}.
Hi, a lead for {brand} on {platform} cost {cpl} in {month}. The return on spend was {roas}.
Hi, on {platform} {brand} had an engagement rate of {eng_rate} against a benchmark of {bench}. We plan a content change.
Hi, {brand} gained {gain} followers on {platform} and reached {reach} people. Growth: {growth}.
Hi, posts of {brand} on {platform} brought {clicks} link clicks (click rate {ctr}). Is your landing page ready?

The engagement rate was {col:goals.er_act} against a goal of {col:goals.er_goal}, which is {col:goals.er_pct}. Status: {col:goals.state}.

Result: {col:exp.state}. We will use this in the next content plan.
Competitor brief for {col:comp.brand}, prepared by {set:firm} on {today}.
{col:comp.competitor} has {col:comp.followers} followers on {col:comp.platform}, posts {col:comp.posts_month} times a month and has an engagement rate of {col:comp.er}.
You have {col:comp.ours} followers there, a share of the audience of {col:comp.share}, and an engagement rate of {col:comp.our_er}. Position: {col:comp.state}.
Our note: {col:comp.note}. We will check this competitor again next quarter.
What we recommend: {col:notes.action}. The owner is {col:notes.owner} and it is due on {col:notes.due}. Status: {col:notes.state}.
Please approve this action or tell us what to change.
Leads and sales from social media for {col:conv.brand}, month of {col:conv.month}, prepared by {set:firm} on {today}.
On {col:conv.platform} you received {col:conv.leads} leads and {col:conv.sales} sales worth {col:conv.revenue}, at an average sale of {col:conv.aov}.
You spent {col:conv.spend}, which is {col:conv.cpl} for each lead and a return of {col:conv.roas} for each unit spent. Result: {col:conv.state}.
The conversion rate from website visits was {col:conv.rate}.
Attribution note for {col:attr.brand}, dated {col:attr.date}, prepared by {set:firm} on {today}.
Source: {col:attr.source}. What happened: {col:attr.note}. We counted {col:attr.leads} leads and {col:attr.sales} sales with revenue of {col:attr.revenue}.
Our confidence is {col:attr.conf}, so the value counted in our reports is {col:attr.value}. Result: {col:attr.state}.
Please confirm this note or tell us if you know a better source.
Audience brief for {col:aud.brand} on {col:aud.platform}, prepared by {set:firm} on {today}.
The largest age group is {col:aud.core}, with {col:aud.core_share} of the audience. {col:aud.women} of your audience are women.

We will write and schedule posts for this audience.

Open Start and type your agency name and your own rules in the yellow cells: a strong and a weak engagement rate, the benchmark tolerance, how close a goal must be and the smallest lift that counts in a test.
Fill Brand Clients with one row for each brand. The followers, reach, engagement rate, goals met and result level fill in from the monthly results.

Every month, enter one row for each client and platform on Monthly Results: followers, followers gained, reach, impressions, engagements, clicks, video views, saves, shares and posts. The rates and the benchmark check fill in.
Keep Benchmarks up to date for each industry and platform. Every monthly result is marked above, on par or below the benchmark using your tolerance.
Enter the posts you want to study on Post Performance. The interactions, engagement rate and level fill in, and Format Performance and Time Of Day use them to show what works best.
Pick the best and worst posts of each month on Top And Bottom Posts, write the lesson and the next action, and let the rate come from the post list.
Set monthly goals on Goals Vs Actual and read the status. Follower Growth shows where new followers come from and how many you lose again.
Record the audience on Audience Demographics, the website visits on Website Traffic and the leads, sales and spend on Conversions And Leads for the cost per lead and the return.
Track competitors on Competitor Tracking and test ideas on Experiments. The share of audience, the position and the winner are worked out for you.
Plan every report on Report Schedule, write the wins, problems and recommendations on Report Notes, and prepare each quarterly meeting on Quarterly Reviews.
Write attribution notes for leads and sales you can trace to a code, link, creator or message, and judge hashtags on Hashtag Performance.

Use the 14 calculators for engagement rate, growth, reach rate, cost per follower, share of voice, goal pacing, best format, benchmark gap, test winner, the report pack, return from social, the quarter forecast, post rank and month change.
Read Analytics Dashboard and Charts every week: reach, engagement rate, goals, overdue reports, leads and revenue.
Ad spend, budgets and results for every client you run ads for
money spent each week for each campaign with the plan, the pace and a flag when a campaign overspends or underspends
a planned budget for each client and month against the money really spent, with what is left and a pace status
your real cost of a lead, a sale, a click or 1,000 impressions on each platform against the target you set
Campaigns by client, platform and objective
every campaign with its spend, leads, sales, revenue, cost per lead and return on ad spend
Client balance and days of money left
top-ups received minus spend gives the balance, and the last 30 days show how many days it lasts before ads stop
a fee by percent, with a minimum or flat, worked out from the real spend each month with the effective rate and what is not yet billed
frequency and the fall in click-through rate show which ads are tired and need a new creative
lookalike and interest tests are compared with the cost per lead target for their platform and marked winner or loser
each tracking item has a result and a recheck date, so wrong tracking is found before it wastes budget
every approval and rejection with the reason and the days to a decision, so you learn what the platforms refuse
conversion rate, load time and lead quality for the pages and forms behind your ads
uses, revenue and the discount given away for each code, with the return from the code worked out in a calculator

One row for each client with a monthly ad budget and your fee rate; spend, leads, revenue, return, cost per lead, balance and days of money left fill in from the spend and results.
One row for each ad account: platform, who pays, daily spend limit and status; campaigns running and spend in the last 30 days against the limit fill in.
One row for each campaign with its daily budget and dates; spend, impressions, clicks, leads, sales, revenue, cost per lead, return and a spend pace flag fill in from the weekly spend and results.
One row for each ad set: audience type, age range, place and daily budget; the client, platform, objective, number of ads and share of the campaign budget fill in.
One row for each ad: format, headline, spend, impressions, clicks and conversions; click-through rate, cost per click, cost per conversion and a verdict against the platform average fill in.
One row for each campaign and week with the money spent and the money planned; the client, platform, objective, month, pace against plan and a flag fill in.
One row for each campaign and month with impressions, clicks, leads, sales and revenue; spend, the result for the objective, cost per result, click rate, cost per click and return fill in.
Budget plan against spend by client and month
One row for each client and month with the planned ad budget; the money spent, what is left, the share used and a pace status fill in from the weekly spend.
One row for each tracking item checked for a client and platform; the days since the check and a status that turns to check due after your recheck days fill in.
One row for each retargeting audience with its source, window, size and the money and leads of the last 30 days; cost per lead and a strong or weak mark fill in.
One row for each audience test with its budget and results; click-through rate, cost per lead, the target for that platform and a verdict of winner, loser or keep testing fill in.
One row for each promo code with its channel, discount, uses and revenue; the average order, the discount given away and whether the code is active fill in.
One row for each landing page with its campaign, visits, conversions and load time; the conversion rate and a strong, weak or slow flag fill in.
Lead forms on the ad platforms
One row for each lead form with its questions, leads, qualified leads and cost; the qualified rate, cost per lead, cost per qualified lead and a strong or weak mark fill in.
Cost per result by objective and platform
One row for each objective and platform with your target cost per result; your real cost, the gap and a within target mark fill in. A result is a lead, sale, click, engagement or 1,000 views.
One row for each ad and week with how often people saw it and its click-through rate; the fall from the first week and a healthy, watch or fatigued status fill in.
One row for each ad sent for platform review with its outcome and reason; days to a decision and an approved, rejected or pending status fill in.
One row for each payment a client makes into their ad budget with its method and status; the brand and month fill in, and received money counts toward the client balance.
One row for each client and month with the fee basis and rate; the spend, the fee and your effective rate fill in, and a billed flag shows what you still need to invoice.
